output.title: Car door inner module pre-assembly

product.name: Car door inner module (trim carrier + subcomponents)
product.description: Pre-assembled door inner module built on a trim carrier about 1.0 × 0.8 m. The carrier holds a window regulator, speaker, and a wiring harness; modules are assembled and then function-tested.

steps.name: PlaceRegulator
steps.does: Place the window regulator onto the carrier and fasten it with 4 screws.

steps.name: FitSpeaker
steps.does: Fit the speaker and fasten it with 3 screws.

steps.name: LayHarness
steps.does: Lay the wiring harness and plug it into the regulator and speaker.

steps.name: FunctionTest
steps.does: Switch on and check the window motor and speaker function.

output.quality: Function test identifies PASS/REJECT; rejected modules are separated for troubleshooting or rework (exact handling not specified).
constraints: Modules ride on fixtures that move with a pallet conveyor.
Target throughput: one module every 90 seconds (takt).
One operator per station; screwdrivers are on balancers; rest of the work is automatic where possible.
Assembly is performed as discrete stations on a single flow line (not a continuous process plant).
assumptions: Shift length is not provided; takt is taken directly from 90 seconds per module, so target is 40 modules/hour.
Carrier/module approximate size is 1.0 × 0.8 m; height is assumed 0.2 m for the digital-twin model because no height was given.
Each of the 4+3 screws is driven by an automatic/assisted screwdriver action at the station with the operator tending/confirming.
Function test time includes switching on and verifying motor and speaker behavior within the station takt budget.

questions.question: What is the approximate module height (or overall Z dimension) on the fixture so the twin model matches the real carrier stack-up?
questions.why: Station clearances and fixture/vacuum/test hardware sizing depend on the module height.

questions.question: Is the 90 seconds/module a hard takt for finished, pass-test modules leaving the last station (i.e., no buffering/rework flow), or does it allow rejects to be handled off-takt?
questions.why: Determines whether test station time must fit strictly into the takt and how buffer/reject handling should be modeled.

questions.question: How do you decide PASS vs REJECT in the function test (e.g., required motor speed/current thresholds, speaker sound/volume check), and what is the disposition of REJECT modules (rework in-line, stand-by, or scrap)?
questions.why: Sets the function test station logic and the downstream routing for bad units.
